page: Amazon Web Services m6id.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is powered by a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor with x86_64 architecture, presenting 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. The configuration includes 16 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Unlike diskless general-purpose variants, the m6id.xlarge integrates a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume. Baseline network throughput is configured at 2 Gbps, and no GPU accelerators are included.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent single-threaded capabilities alongside expected throughput constraints in concurrent workloads. The instance registers mid-tier scores in single-core tests, achieving 1890.49 in stress-ng single-core and 1649.0 in Geekbench single-core, assisted by 54 MB of L3 cache and AVX-512 instruction set support. However, its multi-threaded throughput sits in the bottom quartile, reflecting its two-physical-core ceiling with a Geekbench multi-core score of 3488.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 19.69 GB/sec. Memory bandwidth tests yield 28.15 GB/sec for uncached read operations and 24.59 GB/sec for write operations.

The primary operational tradeoff centers on the inclusion of local NVMe storage versus its modest compute and baseline network profile. The built-in 237 GB NVMe SSD delivers low-latency I/O for temporary data without relying purely on network-attached volumes, offering favorable cost efficiency for workloads requiring fast local scratch space. Given its 2 Gbps baseline network and 4-vCPU envelope, the m6id.xlarge is well positioned for intermediate caching layers, lightweight database replicas, build and CI/CD pipelines needing fast temporary disk, and containerized backend microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m6id.xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 dedicated physical cores on a 3.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8375C processor. Built on the AWS Nitro System, it provides 16 GB of DDR4 memory, a bundled 237 GB NVMe SSD local instance store, and a 2 Gbps baseline network configuration. In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits moderate single-core efficiency, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 1649.0, while multi-threaded capacity remains constrained by its physical core count. The bundled NVMe volume ensures low-latency scratch space without added network storage overhead. This configuration is particularly effective for small-to-medium databases, containerized microservices, CI/CD runners, and caching workloads requiring local high-speed temporary storage.
